title: Natural transformation assembled from characterized sections
statement: For a fixed finite etale $f:Y\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], there is a natural transformation from the functor $F\mapsto f_*f^{-1}F$ to the identity, that is, a family of sheaf morphisms $\tau_F:f_*f^{-1}F\to F$, natural in the abelian sheaf $F$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], such that $\operatorname{LocalSums}(f,F,\tau_F)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-local-sums] for every $F$. No change-of-base assertion is included.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-section-descent] to choose the uniquely characterized $U(F,W,s)$. The zero section satisfies the formulas for zero input. The sum of the sections characterized by $s,s^{\prime}$ satisfies them for $s+s^{\prime}$, because all restrictions are additive and a finite sum distributes over addition. Uniqueness proves that $U$ is an additive homomorphism in $s$.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: For a restriction $k:W^{\prime}\to W$, the restriction of $U(F,W,s)$ satisfies the characterization for $F(B_fk)(s)$: apply its formula to each composite $T\to W^{\prime}\to W$ and use functoriality of $B_f$ and $F$. Uniqueness proves compatibility with restrictions, so the additive component maps give a sheaf morphism $P_F\to F$ with $P_F(W)=F(B_fW)$.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: For a morphism $\varphi:F\to G$, naturality of $\varphi$ commutes with each restriction in the characterization, and its additive components commute with finite sums. Hence $\varphi_WU(F,W,s)$ satisfies the characterization for $G$ and $\varphi_{B_fW}(s)$. Uniqueness gives naturality in $F$. Assemble a natural transformation $P\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: Whisker the natural restriction isomorphism by $f_*$ and compose it with this natural transformation. At each object, its inverse cancels its forward component. The section characterization with $h=\mathrm{id}_W$ and evaluation of a finite sum of group homomorphisms proves the local sum predicate.
